# BAD-006 — Align the iOS App Privacy label with what the app actually collects

## Brief
BADS-004/Charlotte found the live iOS App Privacy label, published around 2026-09-09, over-declares and mis-links against docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-ios-app-review-guest-mode-design.md § 3.3 and docs/MOBILE-STORES.md § B3. It lists Name, Product Interaction, Crash, Performance and Other Diagnostic Data for Analytics, which the phone does not send. It marks every type Not Linked to You, although Email and User ID are the account. It declares Email for Developer's Advertising or Marketing. It omits Coarse Location (the IP-derived heartbeat stamp) and Other User Content (a collab room's scene title).

The signed-in web tree does call the report endpoints (activity, usage), which may count as Product Interaction, linked. So reconcile against the code (web/lib/report.js and the /functions/v1 endpoints the web tree calls) and site/privacy.html before changing anything.

Eric's call (2026-09-14): only the tracking answer changed for the 1.0 resubmission; align the rest after approval.

## Size, persona and model decision
One researcher on fable to reconcile the label with the code and the privacy policy (a wrong declaration is expensive), then a writer driving App Store Connect with Eric's approval for each Publish.
